messages.author: 6d020fc5d7c9ee0a
messages.subject: Issue with Geom_Rect
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to add some shading to a time series plot using geom_rect().  For some reason I keep getting an "Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'y' not found."  This is the code I am running:

rec <- data.frame(x1=c(365,1095,1825), x2=c(730,1460,2190), y1=c(-1,-1,-1), y2=c(1,1,1))


ggplot(pix,aes(x=seq(1:length(pix$y)),y=y)) + geom_point(na.rm=FALSE) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1,365,730,1095,1460,1825), labels = c("2011","2012", "2013", "2014","2015","2016"),limits=c(1,2190))+
  theme_bw() +  geom_rect(data=rec, mapping=aes(xmin=x1, xmax=x2, ymin=y1, ymax=y2), color='grey', alpha=0.2)

I am wondering if there is an issue with my custom scales that are giving me the error?  I've searched a bunch online, but can't seem to find a solution.  Pix is just a  data frame with the time series value, y.

Any advice would be much appreciated.

~Colin

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Issue with Geom_Rect
parts:
As a rule of thumb, you should _never_ include $ in your aes specifications.

Because of the rules of aesthetic inheritance, you also refer to the
variable y in the rect layer, and the rec dataframe doesn't contain a
variable called y. This is easier to spot if you use white space and
indentation to layout your code:

ggplot(pix) +
geom_point(aes(seq_along(y), y)) +
geom_rect(
aes(xmin = x1, xmax = x2, ymin = y1, ymax = y2)
data = rec,
color = 'grey',
alpha = 0.2
)
scale_x_continuous(
breaks = c(1, 365, 730, 1095, 1460, 1825),
labels = 2011:2016,
limits = c(1, 2190)
) +
theme_bw()

(I'm also extremely suspicious of your x axis - aligning arbitrary x
positions to years seems like a recipe for disaster)

Hadley
